urn:eigenius:core:description: Ordinary-differential-equation institution backed by `OrdinaryDiffEq.jl`. v1 scope: validates `OdeSolution` claims by re-integrating the referenced `OdeProblem` with the claimed algorithm + tolerances and confirming the final state matches within tolerance. Future scope (D27 §4.5): `ReproducibleIntegration` claims with trajectory hashing for bit-reproducibility audits, OnDemand `qc_diffeq_solve` exposing on-the-fly integration to FIBER queries, sensitivity analysis, the `Catalyst → DiffEq` comorphism for time-course simulation of reaction networks (the natural pairing for the kinase mechanism the Catalyst tutorial introduces).

Julia entry point that takes an `OdeSolution` mirror struct and returns a `Verdict`. The handler rebuilds the `OdeProblem` from `solution.problem` (parses the RHS source, packs ICs/parameters/tspan), looks up the algorithm in the per-name registry, calls `solve(prob, alg; abstol, reltol)`, checks `successful_retcode(sol)`, and per-component-compares `sol.u[end]` against the claim's `final_state`. Holds on a successful re-integration that matches; Fails on a mismatch or solver-internal failure when success was claimed; Undecidable on indeterminate solver states (`MaxIters`, `ConvergenceFailure`, etc., per D27's verified-API ReturnCode enum).

AutoOnLoad gate fired against every newly committed `OdeSolution` resource. Re-integrates the referenced problem and produces the canonical D14 Verdict tri-state. A `Fails` verdict rejects the gated commit per D31 §6.3 — the chain only persists OdeSolution claims whose final state the institution can independently reproduce.

Julia entry point for the target-side reify of the `Catalyst → DiffEq` Comorphism (D14 §9.3 step 4). The comorphism's typed middle is the identity Lambda on `OdeProblem` (D32 §6.2 generalised) — Catalyst produces a chain-typed `OdeProblem` with FormulaTerm RHS via `compile_to_ode`, and DiffEq speaks the same shape, so the reify is identity at the boundary. The Julia handler returns its `OdeProblem` argument unchanged; the function exists so the kernel's `Exp::InstitutionInvoke` dispatch can route comorphism reify calls through the substrate uniformly with `query` and `extract_typed`, rather than special-casing `no-op` procedures kernel-side.

Typed inbound constructor for `OdeProblem`: reifies a FormulaTerm-typed OdeProblem payload as itself (identity reify — both source and target speak the same shape). Target side of the `Catalyst → DiffEq` comorphism: any institution producing FormulaTerm-typed OdeProblems imports through this format. Anchored on the `reify_problem` Julia handler — the kernel's `ExternalInstitution::reify` dispatches through the substrate the same way `query` does (D14 §9.3 step 4).
